acquisition method: we interrogated the spleen proteome using a label-free shotgun approach
alkylation reagent: Alkylation was achieved using iodoacetamide (GE Healthcare, Little Chalfont, Buckinghamshire, UK)
alkylation concentration: to a final concentration of 9.4 mM at room temperature in the dark, for 30min.
cleavage agent: digestion with MS grade trypsin (Promega, Madison, WI, USA)
collision energy: Selected ions were fragmented by Higher Energy Collision Induced Dissociation (HCD) with a stepped Normalized Collisional Energy (NCE) of 28–30.
fragmentation method: Selected ions were fragmented by Higher Energy Collision Induced Dissociation (HCD)
instrument: The spectral data was acquired using a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific®, Bremen, Germany)
labeling: The Schistosomiasis SpleenOME: Unveiling the Proteomic Landscape of Splenomegaly Using Label-Free Mass Spectrometry
reduction reagent: proteins were reduced using dithiothreitol (Sigma Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA)
reduction concentration: to a final concentration of 3.3 mM at 60°C for 10min.
